clue.text: In European port, closes damaged locks

parts.note: Split is a port on the Croatian coast
closes as a verb means finishes, ends

explanation.surface: Something in a Croatian harbour town shuts down some broken locks on doors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Locks' looks like hardware for doors; it is hair, and the damage is the frayed tips. 'In' merely leads into the port.
explanation.definitionFit: Hair whose strands have frayed and divided at the tips is the classic example of damaged tresses.

clue.text: Ability to go over snow lines

parts.note: to ski is to travel over snow
L is an abbreviation for line, so LL is lines

explanation.surface: The ability to cross snow along marked lines.
explanation.definitionFit: Talent or expertise at doing something well is a learned ability.

clue.text: One's left something to secure entry into shelter

indicators.note: to secure means the shelter word holds the entry word inside

parts.note: lee is the sheltered side, shelter
a gate is a way in, an entry

explanation.surface: Someone has left something to lock the entrance into a shelter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One's left something' reads as someone walking off; it means someone to whom something has been left in a will.
explanation.definitionFit: A beneficiary who inherits under a will is someone bequeathed property.

clue.text: One found in posh port rarely?

definitions.text: One found in posh port rarely?

indicators.note: found in puts the letter for one among the rearranged letters
rarely suggests the words posh port are done in an unusual way, rearranged

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A vessel seldom seen in a smart harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rarely' rearranges POSH PORT into TROOPSHP, and 'found in' puts I inside. As a whole, a military transport is rarely seen in a posh port.
explanation.definitionFit: A vessel carrying soldiers would seldom dock among yachts at a smart marina.

clue.text: Restrictive circles for diners' protection

parts.note: reads like an exclusive dining club guarding its members, but describes table hoops that hold the cloth that shields diners' laps

explanation.surface: Exclusive clubs protect their diners.
explanation.definitionFit: Hoops holding rolled table linen keep the cloth that protects diners' clothes in place.

clue.text: Prescribed a number of games that have their points

definitions.meaning: a ... book is a prescribed text

definitions.text: a number of games that have their points
definitions.meaning: in tennis a ... is a group of games, each scored in points

explanation.definitionFit: A set text is required reading; a tennis set is a sequence of games.

clue.text: Ring back about one feature of bed?

indicators.note: about means the turned word goes round the letter for one
back tells us the word for ring is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: to ring someone is to call them on the phone
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone phones back about one feature of their bedroom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns CALL into LLAC, and 'about' puts I inside it after the first L. The bed is a flower bed, not furniture, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: The flowering shrub with scented purple blooms is a common planting in a garden border.

clue.text: Subsequently shown to be dead right?

parts.note: the late means the dead

explanation.surface: Later shown to be dead right?
explanation.definitionFit: Afterwards, at a following time, means at a subsequent point.

clue.text: Primate concealing old weariness

indicators.note: concealing means the monkey hides the letter for old inside

parts.note: the langur is an Asian monkey, a primate

explanation.surface: An ape hides an old tiredness.
explanation.definitionFit: Listless lethargy or lassitude is a pleasant or heavy tiredness.

clue.text: Given credit, fat man's retrained as an artisan

indicators.note: retrained says the letters of fat man's are trained into a new order

explanation.surface: With a loan, an overweight man retrains as a craftsperson.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retrained' rearranges the letters of 'fat man's', the 's counting as a letter here. 'Given' and 'as' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: A skilled manual worker who makes things by hand is a craftsperson.

clue.text: Popular and mature, rejecting women's clique

parts.note: in means fashionable, popular

indicators.note: rejecting says the letter for women is thrown out of the word for mature

parts.note: to grow up is to mature

explanation.surface: A trendy, grown-up circle turns away the women who would join.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejecting' drops W from GROWUP, leaving the second part.
explanation.definitionFit: An exclusive social circle whose members favour each other is a tight clique.

clue.text: Queen backs own Scots working

indicators.note: backs here is a verb saying the run of letters is turned to face the other way

parts.note: ain is the Scots word for own
at it means busy, working

explanation.surface: A queen supports her own Scottish workers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backs' turns both pieces round together as one run. The Queen is the fairy queen of Shakespeare's A Midsummer Night's Dream, not a real monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's fairy monarch, wife of Oberon in A Midsummer Night's Dream, holds that royal title.

clue.text: Rent increased or decreased?

parts.note: to let a property is to rent it out
up means raised, increased

explanation.surface: A puzzled tenant asks whether the rent went up or down.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke is that pieces meaning 'increased' build a phrase meaning the opposite, so the clue asks if it went up or down.
explanation.definitionFit: To ease off or slacken is a phrasal verb for something becoming less intense.

clue.text: Get into ground, having Rugby training in break

parts.note: to inter is to bury, putting into the ground
RU stands for Rugby Union
PT is physical training

explanation.surface: A player gets mud-stained during rugby training at half-time.
explanation.walkthrough: PT, physical training, is old school gym class.
explanation.definitionFit: To break in on someone talking is to cut across them, a verbal sense of stopping.

clue.text: Anger meant changes in character

parts.note: temper means anger

indicators.note: changes here signals that the letters of meant shift into a new order

explanation.surface: Anger meant changes in someone's personality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changes' rearranges MEANT into AMENT; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A person's nature or disposition is their character.

clue.text: Think pound must be knocked off charge

indicators.note: knocked off says the letter for pound is removed from the word for think

parts.note: to feel something is to believe or think it
L is the abbreviation for a pound, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: A shopper thinks a pound should come off the price.
explanation.definitionFit: A payment demanded for a service, such as a solicitor's bill, is a charge.

clue.text: Cafe's rise possible result of cooking this?

definitions.text: Cafe's rise possible result of cooking this?

indicators.note: cooking signals that the letters are cooked up, shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: A cafe's rising fortunes might come from serving this dish.
explanation.walkthrough: Read backwards: 'cooking' the answer's letters gives CAFES RISE, so the letters of 'Cafe's rise' rearrange to make it. As a whole, a good stew could bring a cafe success.
explanation.definitionFit: A stew of meat in white sauce is a dish a cafe might cook.

clue.text: Madcap owns motor, showing hesitation about drink

indicators.note: about says the word for owns goes around the drink

parts.note: has means owns, possesses
rum is a spirit, a drink
motor is informal for a car
um is the sound of someone hesitating

explanation.surface: A reckless type with a car hesitates over a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' acts on 'owns' and 'drink', though other words stand between them; 'showing' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe someone reckless and wild, behaving impulsively without thought.

clue.text: Emotionally releasing from sectarian movement out of control

parts.note: the Cathars were a medieval religious sect
a tic is an involuntary twitch

explanation.surface: An emotional release from a sectarian movement that's run wild.
explanation.walkthrough: 'movement' looks like part of 'sectarian movement'; it belongs with 'out of control'.
explanation.definitionFit: Purging pent-up feelings brings catharsis, an emotional purge.

clue.text: Write with editor's backing, in order to produce newspaper

indicators.note: in tells us the pieces go inside the word for order

parts.note: to indent for goods is to order them officially

indicators.note: backing turns the editor's abbreviation round

parts.note: ED is the usual abbreviation for editor
to pen is to write

explanation.surface: A journalist writes with an editor's support to get a newspaper out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns the editor round. 'In order' looks like 'so as'; here 'in' is the container word and 'order' is the verb indent (to requisition). The Independent is a British national daily.
explanation.definitionFit: A British national daily paper founded in 1986 carries this title.

clue.text: Insensitive, extreme, and having few prospects

parts.note: dead means numb, insensitive
the end is the extreme point

explanation.surface: Someone numb, extreme and going nowhere.
explanation.definitionFit: A job or road leading nowhere offers no way forward.

clue.text: Have gained after initial reverse

indicators.note: initial reverse says the opening pair of letters is turned round

parts.note: won means gained

explanation.surface: Having gained something after a setback at first.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the first two letters, WO, are turned to OW; N stays put.
explanation.definitionFit: To possess something is to hold it as one's property.

clue.text: Newspaper article about unknown material

indicators.note: about says the newspaper and article wrap around the unknown

parts.note: an organ is a newspaper or periodical
a is the indefinite article
Z is a mathematical unknown

explanation.surface: A newspaper story about an unidentified fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: Z, the algebra unknown, goes between ORGAN and A.
explanation.definitionFit: A thin stiff sheer silk or synthetic fabric used for dresses.

clue.text: Painless effect of son replacing king in an African country

indicators.note: replacing says one letter takes the place of another in the country

parts.note: Algeria is a country in North Africa
R is short for rex, king

explanation.surface: Painkilling results come from a son taking over from the king in an African nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'replacing' swaps the king's letter for the son's in the country; 'an' is kept as written.
explanation.definitionFit: Medical term for absence of pain, the state produced by painkillers.

clue.text: A storm about British housing limit

indicators.note: about says the storm word goes around the abbreviation

parts.note: a gale is a storm

explanation.surface: A storm over British housing restrictions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'housing' looks like the container word; it is part of the definition: the triangular end wall where a house stops.
explanation.definitionFit: The triangular top of a house's end wall marks where the building stops.

clue.text: Protection soldier found in main retreat

indicators.note: found in means the soldier is put inside the turned word
retreat means the word goes backwards

parts.note: the main is a poetic word for the sea
GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: Protection for a soldier in a retreat across the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retreat' turns the sea round, making AES, and 'found in' places the soldier inside it. 'Main' is the old poetic word for the open sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Under the auspices or shield of someone means under their guardianship, a sheltering backing.

clue.text: Cut very thin, say

indicators.note: say tells us to hear the word, not read it

parts.note: sheer means very thin, as with fabric

explanation.surface: Cut very thin, so to speak.
explanation.definitionFit: To clip or trim, as with wool from sheep, is to cut.

clue.text: Refreshing drink in paper container brother's knocked back

indicators.note: container says the paper word holds the other piece

parts.note: a sheet is a piece of paper

indicators.note: knocked back turns the abbreviation backwards

parts.note: BR is the abbreviation for brother

explanation.surface: A brother knocks back a refreshing drink from a paper cup.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocked back' looks like drinking, but turns brother round; 'container' marks the paper as holding it. A sherbet is a sweet fruit drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A cooling sweetened fruit juice drink, originally from the Middle East.

clue.text: Serious complaint about a bill

indicators.note: about says the complaint surrounds the letter a

parts.note: TB is tuberculosis, a serious illness; the run of letters across complaint about is a coincidence

explanation.surface: A serious complaint about a bill.
explanation.definitionFit: A tally or account to pay, as in a bar tab, is a bill.

clue.text: Agreement to double hospital's speciality, a drug

indicators.note: to double says the speciality's letters appear twice

parts.note: ENT is the ear, nose and throat department of a hospital
E is ecstasy, a drug

explanation.surface: A deal is struck to double the hospital's specialist unit and supply a medicine.
explanation.walkthrough: E is crossword shorthand for ecstasy.
explanation.definitionFit: A friendly understanding between nations, as in the Entente Cordiale, is a diplomatic accord.

clue.text: Supply space for printer directly

parts.note: an en is a printer's unit of space
due means directly, as in due north

explanation.surface: A printer is supplied with space right away.
explanation.definitionFit: To endow someone with a quality is to furnish or provide them with it.

clue.text: City University post one holds invalid?

parts.note: Bath is a city in Somerset, England
a chair is a professorship at a university

explanation.surface: A city university job someone holds turns out to be invalid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'invalid' reads as 'not valid' but is a sick person. A bath chair was a hooded wheelchair for the infirm.
explanation.definitionFit: An old-fashioned wheeled seat for carrying a sick person, named after the spa town.
